sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Trump says ban on some news outlets from White House is "because they're fake news" Politico, CNN and MS NOW journalists have been denied access to the White House after US President Donald Trump announced he was banning the outlets .
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: An MS NOW reporter and a photographer tried entering the White House grounds on Saturday morning, but their badges would not scan and an officer confiscated them, the outlet reported.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: Both CNN and Politico also said Saturday morning that their reporters were denied access and had their badges seized.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: Trump said on Friday he was barring all three major US media outlets from the White House, accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: Press freedom advocates called the move unconstitutional.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: "The officer asked me to hand over my badge.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: He said that it was disabled," MS NOW reporter Akayla Gardner said.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: "I asked why I was not able to get inside.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: He said it was above him." Gardner added that while her and her colleague's badges were disabled, an MS NOW producer was still able to scan her badge to get in, though she was not given an explanation as to why the producer's badge still worked.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: CNN reporter Betsy Klein said a Secret Service agent told her her badge had been deactivated.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: Later on Saturday morning, Politico said its reporter Cheyenne Haslett was denied entry and Secret Service revoked her pass.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: All three outlets have spoken out against the decision, accusing Trump of violating their constitutional rights to free speech and freedom of the press.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: An MS NOW spokesperson said in a statement that the White House "belongs to the American people and the decisions made inside are funded by our tax dollars".
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: MS NOW said it "intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy".
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: Politico Editor-in-Chief Jonathan Greenberger said in an internal email, shared in the outlet's Playbook newsletter, that the company stands by its reporters and will "vigorously defend" their First Amendment rights.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: Trump added that there "may be others to join them", but has not given a directive banning additional news outlets.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: When later asked by a reporter what he meant by others to come, Trump responded: "Others to come in terms of fake news?
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: Well, you know, the New York Times is fake news, the Washington Post is fake news." Several groups dedicated to the freedom of the press have called out Trump's White House ban as illegal and unconstitutional.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: A major group that provides legal services to the media - the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press - said it expected Trump's ban to be struck down quickly by the courts because it was "flatly unconstitutional".
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: "The First Amendment is clear that once the White House invites in some journalists, it can't ban others because it doesn't like their reporting," said Bruce Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, which provides legal services to the media.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: It's the latest in a series of moves by the administration to target media outlets Trump says are critical of him, including legal action against US and international outlets like The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, and the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: Some of the lawsuits have resulted in media organisations agreeing to pay multimillion dollar settlements.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: Trump's lawsuit against the BBC is ongoing.
sentences.article_title: Journalists report being denied White House access after Trump bans some outlets

sentences.text: This video can not be played Ed Davey says the Lib Dems have "a historic opportunity to win many more seats and a moral responsibility to stop Reform" Sir Ed Davey said the Liberal Democrats are "a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform" as the party's conference began in Brighton.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: The Lib Dem leader sought to strike a more combative stance as he faced down criticism from his own MPs that the party was struggling for relevance and being too polite about problems.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: On the first day of the autumn conference, Sir Ed warned an "unholy alliance" between Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch and Farage could turn the UK into a "Trump satellite state".
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: Addressing speculation about a possible snap election, he said the party was ready to fight and would build its so-called orange wall even higher by winning more than its 2024 record of 72 MPs.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: Sir Ed's attention-grabbing stunts helped raise the party's profile ahead of the last election, but recent polling showed 43% of respondents were unclear what the Liberal Democrats stand for, with just over half describing them as "weak".
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: South Cotswolds MP Roz Savage criticised Sir Ed's leadership ahead of conference, urging the party to rediscover its "insurgent spirit" rather than being the "polite custodians of a system that leaves people feeling powerless".
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: Speaking on the pebbles of Brighton Beach, Sir Ed dismissed those concerns and told reporters the Liberal Democrats would fight to stop a Reform government.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "One of the things that makes us unique is that we are a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform," he said.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "Many of the seats he needs to get himself into No 10 are seats that we will defend and indeed win - and we are also able to take seats off the Conservatives, because I really fear that Kemi Badenoch will give the keys to No 10 to Nigel Farage, so we have got to stop the Conservatives as well.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "We have got an historic opportunity to win many more seats and a moral responsibility to stop Reform." He added a manifesto working group had already been set up in case of an early election "so we'll be ready if it comes early, but, you know, it still could be up to three years away".
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: Sir Ed insisted his party has a "distinctive position" in British politics, and will use the four-day conference to position it to take on the challenge from Reform as well as its typical rivals the Conservatives, talking up their focus on the NHS and goal of re-joining the EU single market and customs union.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: The Lib Dem leader highlighted how six former Conservative cabinet ministers were among 25 Tories to have defected to Reform in the last two years, claiming they were now competing with each other to see who can divide the country more, rather than looking to fix the country's problems.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "An unholy alliance between Farage and Badenoch is the only way either can get into power," he said.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "Together, they want to turn Britain into a Trump satellite state which would trash our NHS, turn our communities against each other, cause untold damage to our environment, and trample over traditional British values of fairness, tolerance, and decency.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: Parents could lose their benefits or face prison sentences for their children's crimes under reforms to the youth justice system, a minister has said.

sentences.article_title: Parents could lose benefits or face prison for child's crimes, minister says

sentences.text: Richards said prison sentences would only apply "in the most extreme cases" and would be up to judges' discretion.
sentences.article_title: Parents could lose benefits or face prison for child's crimes, minister says

sentences.article_title: Parents could lose benefits or face prison for child's crimes, minister says

sentences.article_title: Parents could lose benefits or face prison for child's crimes, minister says

sentences.text: "Yes, that will have some stick.

sentences.article_title: Parents could lose benefits or face prison for child's crimes, minister says

sentences.text: Cami Sophia sees September as a chance to get ahead with her goals The lazy hazy days of summer may feel like a distant memory as September shifts our energy back to business and forward to new adventures.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: It's the month when many of us embark on a new chapter, whether it's university, college or a new job or simply getting back to work and the school run.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: It's also the time that "September Reset" trends on social media - the kind, chill sister of New Year's Resolutions.
sentences.article_title: Why I'm doing a September reset and how you can create a new routine

sentences.text: The dinghy carried 165 migrants across the English Channel on 23 July A teenager who piloted a dinghy carrying a then-record 165 migrants across the English Channel to the UK has been sentenced to two years and three months in prison.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: Chan Mathok Atak, 19, from South Sudan, admitted endangering others during a sea crossing on 23 July - the 16th conviction since the new offence was created in January.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: Prosecutors at Canterbury Crown Court said Atak created a risk of death or serious personal injury to others on board the boat.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: At the time, the so-called "mega dinghy" set a record for the largest number of migrants brought over on a small boat in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: That figure has since been surpassed with 230 people on board a vessel in August .
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: At Canterbury Crown Court on Friday, Judge Sarah Counsell said the offence was so serious "only an immediate custodial sentence can be justified".
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: She warned Atak that as a foreign national he was liable in principle to automatic deportation once he completed his sentence.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: James Harrison, prosecuting, told the court the boat Atak was piloting was 12.8ft (3.9m) wide and 46.9ft (14.3m) long, a similar length to a standard bus.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: The boat had travelled between Calais and the UK and was deflating when it was picked up by border force vessels.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: Chan Mathok Atak admitted endangering others during a sea crossing The dinghy, which had 31 children on board with the youngest aged 14, had two outboard engines but one was not working, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: The National Crime Agency (NCA) said the boat was "severely overcrowded", had limited food, drinking water, and medication, and had been at sea for almost 24 hours.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: The quality of the lifejackets on board was also "completely inadequate" and the fire risk was "considerable" due to how close batteries were to fuel cans, the NCA added.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: Harrison said just before the boat was intercepted, Atak moved away from the engine into another part of the vessel and took off his jacket.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: This video can not be played Atak was seen piloting the boat during 90 minutes of aerial footage He said this was an attempt to not to be identified as the helmsman.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: However, Atak was seen during 90 minutes of aerial footage to be piloting the vessel using its one remaining functioning engine while wearing a black jacket with an "Italia" logo on it, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: Footage also showed one person "constantly pumping" to try to re-inflate the rigid-hulled inflatable boat.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: Harrison said: "There's no evidence to suggest that the defendant had any training or experience of conducting this type of navigation.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: "The size of the vessel and the number of people on board presented an obvious danger.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: The vessel would have been unstable because of it deflating." Harrison said the risks of the crossing "would have been apparent to Atak".
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: In an interview, Atak said he paid €200 euros (£172) to a gang for the crossing but denied he was the helmsman.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: NCA senior investigating officer John Turner said: "Atak was unimaginably reckless and his actions could have easily resulted in many deaths had this boat not been intercepted.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: "Not only did he place the lives of 165 migrants in severe peril, this flimsy vessel was entirely unsuitable for crossing one of the world's busiest shipping lanes." Endangerment at sea was made a new offence this year to target those alleged to have steered small boats over the Channel.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: Anna Turley, Minister for Border Security and Asylum, described Atak as an "evil criminal".
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: "He joins 16 other pilots sentenced in just three months for endangering lives with flimsy, overcrowded dinghies," she said.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: "The idea that he had anything to do with the state of the boat and its overcrowding just flies in the face of reason," she added.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: Mogan described Atak as someone who had "escaped the horrors of South Sudan", where he saw people being shot and having their throats cut, and militia setting fire to a neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed

sentences.text: Rob Griffin was appointed substantively into the role of deputy chief constable, Nottinghamshire Police said The father of a student who was stabbed to death in the Nottingham attacks has criticised a move by Nottinghamshire Police to promote the senior officer who led the investigation.

sentences.text: Grace O'Malley-Kumar, Barnaby Webber and Ian Coates were stabbed on 13 June 2023 by Valdo Calocane, leading to a public inquiry .

sentences.text: Rob Griffin, of Nottinghamshire Police, was temporary deputy chief constable from 29 April 2025 and was appointed substantively into the role following a selection process in August, the force said.
sentences.article_title: Nottingham attacks family condemn police promotion

sentences.text: Sanjoy Kumar, Grace's dad, told the BBC on Friday: "I think this is completely wrong." Police say the process consisted of an application form, a people panel and external advisors.

sentences.text: Griffin has previously been described by Barnaby's mother Emma Webber as having "blood on his hands" , following the force's failure to detain Calocane, who had been diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020, after an arrest warrant was issued in September 2022.

sentences.text: "Furthermore, he didn't let us know about the professional standards investigations that were taking place." Kumar said families would have expected people appointed in senior police roles, such as the deputy chief constable, to have "candour and integrity".

sentences.text: "We clearly felt that lacking in this case," he added.

sentences.text: He said he wanted to ask the secretary of state responsible for policing in the UK and the policing minister "what on earth is going on here?" He added: "This is not someone who is reliable, this is someone who misled victims in a horrific situation.

sentences.text: "This is a person who lacked candour and integrity from our point of view.

sentences.text: James and his partner have been unable to sell their one-bedroom flat in London and say they are on the verge of bankruptcy In 2015, thousands of people queued overnight in the rain to reserve and buy studio apartments selling for under £200,000 in Hounslow, west London.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: It's in stark contrast to today's appetite for flats, with property portals reporting a slump in sales.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: But why, when the country is in a housing crisis with a desperate need for affordable homes , are flats now struggling to sell?
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: According to the property site Zoopla, 88% of flats listed for sale in inner London on its website in 2025 did not find a buyer within six months.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: The company also says the gap between the value of a flat and a house is the widest it has been for 30 years.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: Executive director Richard Donnell points to post-pandemic social changes with "people looking for space, prioritising houses, working from home".
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: He also points to higher mortgage rates, people concerned about "all the costs and liabilities of owning a property" including service charges and ground rents.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: In September, nearly all the major mortgage lenders in the UK announced increases in the cost of home loans.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: Donnell says flats in inner London are struggling in particular as they are more expensive, the service charges are higher, and "there's greater complexity - it's highly likely it's a bigger building, maybe more of a complex building, so less are selling within six months".
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: This is a message echoed by property platform Rightmove, which says as of August, only 50% of flats listed for sale nationally successfully find a buyer, compared to 65% of houses.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: Nationally, as of August, the average price for a flat is down 2% from 12 months prior.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: That is the largest drop seen over the period by any type of property.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: Compared with August 2021, flats have only risen in price by 4% nationally, the least of all property types.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: Colleen Babcock, Rightmove's head of partner marketing, says London faces additional challenges because its market is heavily weighted towards flats, and "affordability more broadly remains a key challenge".
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: She points to higher borrowing costs, increased stamp duty costs , and the limitations of the Lifetime ISA in higher-priced areas, which mean both first-time buyers and home-movers in London can face additional hurdles when buying a home.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: Flats aren't becoming unsellable for one single reason.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: Higher borrowing costs, service charges, leasehold and shared ownership complications have made them more expensive and complicated to own, damaging their reputation.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: James Schaife, 36, says he and his partner are "on the verge of bankruptcy" after struggling to sell their one-bedroom north London flat for the past four years.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: He bought a 35% share of the £585,000 flat - run by Newlon Housing Trust - in 2017, but after his partner got a new job, James moved out of London in 2022 and relocated north, putting the flat on the market.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: Within an initial "nomination period" - a set window of time where the association has the exclusive right to find an eligible buyer - the flat generated next to no interest.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: The housing association gave them permission to sell it on the open market - but James claims they have been "forced to use a narrow selection of valuers chosen by Newlon", despite estate agents telling him the flat has been overvalued.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: They have been forced to rent out the property with a special "consent-to-let" agreement with their housing association - although this is due to expire imminently and James claims Newlon will not renew it.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: James said the situation has affected their plans to start a family, pushing them back to an age "where it's probably unlikely that we'll have children".
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: "It's just ruined our lives." A spokesperson for Newlon Housing Trust said that "this is not a picture we recognise", adding that they were bound by "strict rules about resales to protect the public purse".
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: The spokesperson said that "strict rules to limit subletting... prevent the risk of people profiting by letting subsidised affordable housing".
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: "As is well reported, the sales market is flat.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: It may be a more extreme example, but many find themselves in this position.
sentences.article_title: 'Our flat has been for sale for four years': Why is the market so weak?

sentences.text: Sophie Bichener, leaseholder and campaigner with the End our Cladding Scandal group, said that flats with unsafe cladding left unremediated were like "prisons", and this is having a "devastating" impact on people's lives.

sentences.text: Thousands of passengers were delayed by the NATS outage An air traffic control failure that sparked widespread travel chaos earlier this month was caused by a "software defect" affecting the system underpinning UK air space management, the national air traffic service Nats has said.

sentences.text: The couple are aware of the risks that come with their no-deposit mortgage Until last year, Conroy, 32, and his partner Amber, 28, saw little prospect of owning their own home.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Freddo the robot in action at Vsim Freddo the robot walks across the office and takes a plastic bottled offered by a staff member.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Given that a robot recently beat Usain Bolt's 100m sprint record, it's not the most startling achievement.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But the speed by which Freddo has been trained to walk, recognise the bottle and grasp it is impressive.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It took just a few minutes to develop those skills and upload them to Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: His developers say rival systems could take days to attain such skills.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: I'm at Vsim, a British start-up based in Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey hope one day their software will control robots that can navigate and do useful tasks in the home and workplace.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But there's a long way to go.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It's a weird situation with robotics because actually the stuff that we find as humans to be incredibly difficult, like gymnastics, you can get robots to do reasonably well.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The stuff that humans are really good at, like fine dexterity, is really hard in robots," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Vsim founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey Freddo's skills were honed in a virtual environment, where a task can be performed  in a computer simulation millions of times.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Once the optimum solution (known as a policy) is found, it can be uploaded and used by the hardware - in this case Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Such virtual simulations are a common way to train robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Tech giant Nvidia has a system called Isaac Sim which works that way - Lu and Storey both worked on an early version of it.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: In 2022 they decided to set up Vsim, to build the their own training system environment and other tools.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: As they were starting from scratch Lu and Storey could optimise the software to exploit the powerful computer chips used in AI, known as graphics processing units or GPUs.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "The underlying algorithms that we were using for most of these robotic simulations they hark back to the 1970s and 1980s, but those algorithms are not really brilliant fits for GPUs," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Within months they realised their system could work much faster than anything they had seen before.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Eighteen months in and we actually have a completely functional, super high-performance simulator," says Lu.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The software is so efficient that it can run on the hardware carried by Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That means the robot can run tens of thousand of simulations while it is moving around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It can look about a second, or so, ahead into the future for 20,000 different kind of combinations of things that might happen," Storey explains.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And that would be vital for a robot moving around an unstructured environment like the average home.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Things outside of the robot's control, like humans, animals or even other robots, could do things that require a change of strategy.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: These unexpected events could happen very quickly and the robot needs to be able to quickly adapt to ensure its actions remain safe and on-mission," Lu says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Robot training systems use virtual environments where tasks are practised Vsim is a start-up with 10 engineers working on its tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It does not build robots, instead it has a suite of software designed to let organisations train and control robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The problem is when you start doing long-horizon tasks, where I say: 'I want you to take the bottle and I want you to fill it up and I want you to go pour'," says Spencer Huang, director of product for robotics at Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: New Yorkers, and LinkedIn's Nicole Leverich, share their networking tips For some, networking comes naturally but for others, the thought of approaching someone they don't know and trying to make a professional connection can fill them with dread.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Whether you're looking for your first job, trying to get ahead at work or hoping to change career, building a network can help you find opportunities and make connections.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Networking doesn't have to mean working a room at a formal event - it can happen in person over a coffee at work, through a chance conversation or online, through email and social media.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Just under half (44%) of Gen Z say not having the right network is the biggest barrier to landing an entry-level role, according to research from LinkedIn , external .
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Nicole Leverich, chief communications officer at LinkedIn, shares her top tips on how to network and we took the same question to city workers in New York to find out what has worked for them.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Everyone can start building their network online and "you'd be surprised how many connections you have once you connect with people you went to school with, former professors, people you met through summer jobs, family and friends," says Leverich.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Don't be discouraged if your network is small as "not having a network right now doesn't mean you'll never have a network", she says.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: And not having obvious industry contacts shouldn't put you off.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Leverich grew up in a small town in Oregon and moved to San Francisco after college without knowing anyone who worked in communications.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: In a message you should "reference something they've posted or establish some common ground".
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Make sure your request is "clear and specific" and something they can do in less than five minutes.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: And, most importantly, don't forget to say thank you.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: "You'd be surprised by how many people are willing to help, but I get so few thank yous," she says.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: "I'm not talking about anything excessive but just a 'thanks' makes you want to help next time." Networking can feel transactional, so to avoid that, try to build relationships before you need something from them, Leverich advises.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: If you know you want to work in a particular industry, "start finding people in that field a year or two before you're looking for a job".
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: When you reach out to them, think about what you can offer them in return.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: "If you call me and say you want a job randomly, I'm much less likely to help than if you call and ask for five minutes of advice." You also don't have to start by messaging someone directly, she says.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Instead you could react to a post or drop a comment.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: In-person networking can be more daunting, particularly early in your career, but remember that at a networking event, everyone is there to talk.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: To begin a conversation, start with something simple like complimenting someone's outfit, introducing yourself and asking why they're there, Leverich advises.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: There is no broader articulation of what a vision for Liberal Britain is." Even those most loyal to Davey admit the party was struggling to offer a clear and coherent message.

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to reform adult social care in England Prime Minister Andy Burnham is facing calls to set a national waiting-time target for dementia care in England.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: An Alzheimer's Society proposal to set an 18‑week referral‑to‑treatment target has been backed by Professor Sir Mike Richards, England's former national cancer director, and Baroness Louise Casey, who's leading a major review of adult social care.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: In a report, Alzheimer's Society and the King's Trust said a "cancer-style revolution" was needed to improve dementia care, which they described as being "stuck in the 20th century".
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: In a speech at Alzheimer's Society conference on Thursday, Social Care Minister Alison McGovern expressed support for the report , external .
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: She said: "The report that the Alzheimer's Society published today on going on the journey that we've been on with cancer, with Alzheimer's and dementia, I think that's spot on." The minister said dementia had been "neglected for far too long".
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: McGovern said the government would "appoint a dementia tsar, backed with real expertise".
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: Currently there is no waiting-time target for dementia in England.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: In contrast, the NHS sets waiting-time targets for cancer diagnosis and treatment.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: Professor Richards was the national cancer director when these cancer targets were introduced in 2000, and said he thought an 18‑week referral‑to‑treatment target for dementia patients was achievable.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: He said setting such a target would require "political initiative" and extra funding.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: "All of that is going to cost more money but remember the toll that this condition is taking at the moment, both on the people affected by dementia themselves and their relatives," the professor said.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: The same proposal has been made by Baroness Casey.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: In a letter to former Health Secretary Wes Streeting in March, she said the government should look at "how dementia can be put on a level playing field with other conditions, for example by setting national standards for dementia diagnosis, including an 18‑week referral‑to‑treatment target".
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC, Baroness Casey said she agreed with the proposal to emulate cancer care.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: About one million people are living with dementia in the UK, a figure expected to reach 1.4 million by 2040.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: Returning from compassionate leave, he said his father would have wanted him "back out there" to bring forward "the changes that he always pushed me to make".
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: In July, Burnham spoke about his father's condition and said it had influenced his drive to reform adult social care in England.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham urged to set dementia waiting-time target

sentences.text: Burnham has said he will wait for Baroness Casey's recommendations before deciding what changes to make to social care and how it's funded.

sentences.text: Andy Haldane, who has advised Burnham on the economy, claimed financial markets had grown wary of his economic plans and now considered his premiership a "traditional tax and spend socialist government".

sentences.text: But the PM rejected this, adding that he would not take risks with the economy and had already made difficult choices since taking office.

sentences.article_title: Burnham rejects 'tax and spend socialist' comments

sentences.text: In an interview with LBC , external on Tuesday, he urged him not to raise taxes further, but said investors were questioning whether he was prepared to risk anger from Labour backbenchers by making reductions in public expenditure.
sentences.article_title: Burnham rejects 'tax and spend socialist' comments

sentences.text: "The fiscal Achilles Heel of this government thus far has been its unwillingness and/or inability to cut public spending," he told the radio station.
sentences.article_title: Burnham rejects 'tax and spend socialist' comments

sentences.text: "Within financial markets, we've gone from the cautious optimism of the summer months to the studied scepticism of September.
sentences.article_title: Burnham rejects 'tax and spend socialist' comments

sentences.text: But he rejected Haldane's characterisation of how markets viewed the government, telling broadcasters: "That doesn't tell the story.
sentences.article_title: Burnham rejects 'tax and spend socialist' comments

sentences.text: We are not that." He added he had already taken difficult decisions on public spending, including "reprioritising" some government spending over the summer to pay for his early cost of living announcements , and scrapping the rollout of digital ID.
sentences.article_title: Burnham rejects 'tax and spend socialist' comments

sentences.text: He added: "So it's not the case that we aren't going to take difficult decisions.
sentences.article_title: Burnham rejects 'tax and spend socialist' comments

sentences.text: We will take difficult decisions to make sure the economy remains on track." Burnham said government efforts to lower living costs would "need to continue", adding that rises to inflation were a "concern".

sentences.text: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage pictured during the party's annual party conference earlier this month The £72m heading towards Reform UK's coffers from two British billionaires is transforming the debate at Westminster about politics and money.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: In short, how should political parties be paid for, and by who?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: And, what is a legitimate donation and what isn't?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: The government is planning to tighten residency rules for people giving money to political parties, to ensure that those making significant donations live in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: But it is worth setting out the law, in broad terms, now and how the government hopes to change it.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Right now, there is no limit on how much anyone, living in the UK or abroad, can give to a British political party as long as the individual is registered to vote in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: But the government has been planning a change in the law for months, which would limit donations from Brits abroad to £100,000 each per year, backdated to 25 March this year.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: But, crucially, the law hasn't changed yet and some of the key details in that proposed new law - such as what residency requirements would need to be passed to be classified as no longer being abroad - haven't been decided yet.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: The reason for that date, 25 March, ministers argue, is that is the day a review by the retired civil servant Philip Rycroft was published, , external the first recommendation of which was that there should be "an annual cap on political donations from British voters living abroad".
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: On that same day, the then-cabinet minister Steve Reed told the Commons , external that cap would be £100,000 per year.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: He also added that it would "apply retrospectively" from that date onwards, even though the law at the time, and indeed now, has not yet changed.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Two big questions arise from this plan: is it proportionate to limit what British folk abroad can donate to UK political parties, given they are arguably less invested in the country than people living here?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: And is it unfair, even morally questionable, to pass a law, but then backdate when its impact begins?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Fast forward to the last few days and along come these colossal donations from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, two cryptocurrency billionaires who until recently lived in Hong Kong and Thailand respectively.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: They have both now returned to the UK.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: In his first interview since these donations became public, Nigel Farage told me unequivocally that the money from both men was legal under the law as it stands now.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: But he was equivocal when I asked him if they would be legal under the law the government hopes to pass shortly.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: "Both these donations are 100% compliant with the law today, of that there is no question whatsoever," Farage told me.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Ah, today, I pointed out.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: This video can not be played Farage: Donations to Reform '100% compliant with the law today' We don't know, because Reform won't tell us, precisely when the two men relocated to the UK.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Nor do we know, because the government hasn't decided yet, what relocating - residency - would look like legally.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Would it be being on the electoral roll at a UK address?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Would it be being resident in the UK for tax purposes?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: In other words the hurdles they plan, while still ill-defined, look like they might be quite high - and folk in government, publicly and privately, are leaning into making that point.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Farage picked a scrap with them in his interview with me, and the government is hitting back.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Do Delo and Harborne clear them, and if they don't, for how long could that delay Reform getting hold of their vast sums of money?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: The Reform UK leader has threatened that a Reform government would cut off party funding from the trades unions if the government went ahead with trying to limit his capacity to raise money from these two donors.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Who is Reform donor and crypto billionaire Ben Delo?

sentences.text: So, there are loads of questions that tumble towards us after these donations.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Should there be a limit on the proportion of a party's funding that can come from one individual?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Should there be a limit on what donors based in the UK can give per year, as well as a cap on donations from Brits abroad?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: The General Secretary of the Unite union has suggested a domestic cap somewhere between £500,000 and £1m a year.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Some argue this would compel parties to find their funding via lots of small donations rather than fewer giant ones.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Former consultant hopes Letby inquiry recommendations will prevent deaths happening again One of the senior doctors who tried to raise concerns about Lucy Letby with hospital managers has told the BBC the final inquiry report makes for "grim reading".
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Consultant paediatrician Dr John Gibbs worked at the Countess of Chester Hospital throughout the period in 2015 to 2016 when Letby murdered seven babies, and attempted to murder seven more, on the neonatal unit.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: He said that he accepted that consultants must bear "collective" responsibility for some of the failings identified in the report.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "I wish we consultants had been brave enough to follow our suspicions and escalate things to the police earlier," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "When I say, 'we consultants', I am responsible as well and if my other consultant colleagues didn't go to the police, I should have." The Thirlwall Inquiry was launched after former nurse Letby was convicted in 2023, and the final report was published on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: In the 822-page document, Lady Justice Thirlwall described "a complete failure to protect babies on the neonatal unit at the Countess of Chester Hospital".
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: The report found that the police "should have been notified earlier than they were" and that hospital managers had repeatedly dismissed consultants' concerns.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Reflecting on the findings for the first time, Gibbs said: "I wasn't expecting it to be an easy read and it certainly isn't.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: I'd imagine it's an extremely difficult read for the parents of the babies concerned.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "But it was during that 11 months after Lucy Letby was moved off the unit, before the police got involved, that it was a very difficult atmosphere, very tense, very stressful dealing with the managers," he added.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Managers "were determined to ensure that we accepted Lucy Letby had been wrongly suspected of doing any harm," the senior doctor explained.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: He also spoke of the failures of his and his wider team, specifically referencing a doctor who disregarded blood test results that suggested a baby had been poisoned with insulin in August 2015.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: While one of his colleagues had missed the relevance of the results when they came back from the lab, it had been a collective team failure, Dr Gibbs concluded.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "Others of us were on call and covering the neonatal unit over the next week or two before the baby moved out of the unit.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: We all had the opportunity to review the notes." Letby, who maintains her innocence, is serving 15 whole-life terms for the murders and has twice been denied permission to appeal against her convictions.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: The Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC), an independent body set up to examine potential miscarriages of justice, is currently reviewing her convictions.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: The inquiry looked into the actions of managers at the hospital where Lucy Letby worked In the weeks and months after Letby was convicted, questions about the case arose in the form of online conspiracy theories and discourse from serious academics, including medical experts and statisticians.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Gibbs said that the continuing support for Letby had taken a toll on him and other consultants, and that claims she had been wrongly convicted were "frustrating and difficult" to hear.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "I particularly find the misinformation that's on the internet is difficult to deal with," he said.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: He added: "I haven't changed my mind that I think Lucy Letby is guilty." However, he emphasised that, because of the "calibre of some of the people who've raised concerns", it is "important" that the evidence used to convict Letby is being examined by the CCRC.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Thirlwall's report called for a series of urgent reforms to neonatal units, including CCTV for all cots and incubators, and restricting access to insulin.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: After the report was published, Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said officials will "urgently develop plans" to introduce live-streaming cameras on England's baby wards.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Thirlwall said some of the babies Letby killed could have been saved if managers at the Countess of Chester Hospital had taken action earlier.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Letby was moved on to administrative duties in July 2016 after consultants expressed concerns about her to the hospital's executive team.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: But the inquiry has found that alarm bells should have been sounded earlier.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: There were several "missed opportunities" for hospital bosses to intervene, the report said, including when three babies died in one cluster in June 2015.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: The key findings and recommendations from the Lucy Letby report Parents of the babies were "kept in the dark for years" over the concerns that their babies might have been deliberately harmed, the inquiry also found.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Thirlwall described the lack of consideration shown to parents as "reprehensible".
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Hospital bosses carried out a number of internal reviews into increased infant mortality in 2015 and 2016, but did not invite Cheshire Police to investigate until May 2017.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Letby remained on site until her arrest more than a year later.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: The public inquiry into the Lucy Letby case may have reserved the strongest criticism for the Countess of Chester Hospital and its management, but there are big questions for the wider NHS to answer too.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: The Thirlwall inquiry's final report , external said there was a "complete failure" to protect babies on the neonatal unit where Letby murdered seven and attempted to murder seven more.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: But a third of the report was given over to the wider role played by the health system in England - and make no mistake, it was found lacking.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: Across more than 200 pages, inquiry chair Lady Justice Thirlwall set out how the culture of the health system created the conditions that enable poor care - or in this case criminality - to go unchecked for so long.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: The failures encompass everything from regulation and employment practices to the way the NHS and government struggle to learn the lessons of the past.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: They have prompted Health Secretary Yvette Cooper to say she "will not hesitate" to hold the system to account at every level.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: She has promised to set up a hub to track the progress on implementing the inquiry's recommendations and pointed to the creation of a new maternity and neonatal commissioner post as a sign of her commitment to improving standards.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: "This must be a turning point for the NHS," she told the House of Commons when responding to the publication of the report.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: The inquiry said NHS managers have become pre-occupied with avoiding blame, leading to an "over-focus on process and reputation management".
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: One witness described this as "blame engineering", with the inquiry concluding this was a key characteristic in the way Countess of Chester bosses approached the Letby case with the report describing it at one point as an "exercise in spin".
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: Letby is serving 15 whole-life prison terms for murdering seven babies and attempting to murder seven more.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: She was convicted in 2023 and has twice been denied permission to appeal against her convictions This weakness means raising the alarm becomes difficult - a concern that has been repeated again and again in inquiries into other scandals.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: There have been plenty of initiatives to address this over the years.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: In the last decade, this has taken the form of the Freedom to Speak Up programme with each NHS organisation having a "guardian" whose job is it to support staff who want to issue a concern.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: But in a number of places the initiative has become a "box ticking" exercise The result?
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: A "toxic negativity" persists around whistleblowing with staff discouraged from speaking out, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: This view is supported by the most recent NHS staff survey , external which showed a declining confidence in speaking out.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: There is, the Thirlwall inquiry said, a consistent inability within the NHS to deal with poor performance.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: Failing managers will be moved, often with the active assistance of NHS England, in a process referred to as rehabilitation, the inquiry heard.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: Countess of Chester chief executive Tony Chambers referred to it as "the donkey sanctuary".
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: The report even noted how some failing managers receive pay offs and move on elsewhere "with few questions asked" as NHS trusts worry about the threat of employment tribunals.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: While there are many excellent managers in the NHS, profound change is needed in the way the NHS deals with those who fail, the inquiry added.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: The government wants to bring in a barring service, but the inquiry warned this will be undermined if the system continues to turn a blind eye like it does.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: In its closing submission to the inquiry, NHS England said it would never "knowingly" move "bad apples" into other jobs, but did believe moving capable senior managers could help improve services where improvement was needed as well as develop individuals.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: Key findings from Lucy Letby Thirlwall Inquiry Regulation has also been found lacking.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: The Care Quality Commission (CQC) inspected the Countess of Chester in February 2016 - Letby carried on attacking babies until June of that year.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: Key information was withheld from inspectors, but the regulator was criticised for not showing enough curiosity to look beyond what they were being told.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: Only a year before, the CQC had been warned by another inquiry into baby deaths at Morecambe Bay NHS Trust that it needed to take a tougher approach.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: Weaknesses have persisted since, the Thirwall inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: An independent review in 2024 warned the ability of the CQC to spot poor performance was by that point deteriorating.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: The CQC has released a statement acknowledging it was not investigative or inquiring enough in 2016, but said it had since strengthened its approach.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Nursing and Midwifey Council, which regulates nurses, was also told it should have been more curious - it renewed Letby's registration at a time when she was not permitted to work on a ward and a police investigation was taking place.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: It has offered an apology in response to the criticisms.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: As part of its work, the inquiry looked at why the lessons of previous inquiries have not been learned.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: There has been countless inquiries dating back 30 years, with thousands of recommendations made.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: But the Thirwall inquiry said most of these have not been implemented - and, when they have, it has taken too long or progress has not been tracked.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: It blamed, among other things, a lack of political will and disruption caused by repeated structural reorganisations.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: This had a potentially significant impact in the Letby case, the inquiry suggested.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: It cited the medical examiner system, whereby an independent doctor looks into deaths that are not reviewed by a coroner so that the cause of death is not down to the doctor involved in the patients care to sign off.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: The move was recommended in 2003 by the inquiry into the Harold Shipman murders and called for again a decade later as part of the inquiry into the failings at Mid Staffordshire NHS Trust.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: But it took until 2024 for it to be introduced.
sentences.article_title: Letby failings go beyond one hospital - the whole system has been found lacking

sentences.text: Former health secretary Sir Jeremy Hunt told the inquiry he believes it would have prevented a number of deaths at the Countess of Chester if it had been in place sooner.

sentences.text: You wake up feeling unwell but there's a big day at work ahead.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: If the answer is to go in (or log on), you're not alone.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: Research suggests , external anywhere between a third to a half of people in the UK work even when sick - something experts call presenteeism.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: And your approach to sickness says a lot about you as an individual and where you work.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: "The younger generation get the snowflake tag thrown at them, but it's not true," says University of Manchester psychologist Prof Sir Cary Cooper, who is one of the world's leading experts on workplace wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: Data from the Office for National Statistics , external supports this view.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: Workers aged 16 to 24 took an average of 2.4 days off sick last year, compared to 6.2 days for those aged 50 to 64.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: Sir Cary, who has advised the UK government on employment policies in this area, says there are several reasons for this.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: Younger workers are more likely to work in roles where there is little security, such as zero-hours contracts.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: They are also less likely to suffer from long-term health conditions and joint problems that are major contributors to sickness absence.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: But Sir Cary adds: "I think younger generations do have higher expectations about how employers should treat them and consider their wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: "Older generations have perhaps been more willing to put up with things, but that doesn't necessarily make that approach healthy.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: "When it comes to taking time off, younger workers seem more willing to view mental wellbeing as part of their overall health rather than something that should simply be pushed through." There are a variety of factors that influence someone's approach to sickness absence.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: For some, work is closely tied to identity.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...
