sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: "These people feel a strong desire to keep showing up," says Dr Audrey Tang, a psychologist who writes about workplace wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: She says those working in caring professions such as medicine, nursing and teaching have a particular tendency towards this.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: "They're more likely to be early in their profession and they don't want to leave a negative impression." Workplace culture and behaviour can have a significant influence on people's willingness to take time off sick, says psychologist Dr Tara Quinn-Cirillo.
sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.article_title: Do you feel guilty when calling in sick at work? This might be why...

sentences.text: More than 24,000 Covid vaccine-harm claims have been made - most relating to the AstraZeneca jab The government scheme to support people injured by Covid vaccines and other jabs has cost £83m to run since April 2022, new figures have revealed.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The amount spent on administration costs and medical assessments is more than double the £32m paid out in financial support to victims so far.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The Taxpayers' Alliance think tank said the public would be "stunned" at the cost and called for the government to urgently review the scheme.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: NHSBSA which runs the scheme for the government says rising numbers of claims are behind the increasing administrative and medical assessor supplier costs.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: Firm assessing Covid vaccine harm replaced after costs spiral to £48m Families failed by Covid jabs tell inquiry of pain The latest data , external shows there have been 24,260 claims since November 2021, although just 264 have been successful.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The Vaccine Damage Payment Scheme (VDPS) was set up in 1979 to provide financial support to people who, in rare cases, had been harmed by vaccines of any type.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: Since the pandemic the number applying for damage payments has increased sharply.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The vast majority of applications are now linked to the AstraZeneca vaccine and other Covid jabs.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The benefits of vaccination are well documented.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The AstraZeneca Covid jab is credited with saving millions of lives worldwide.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: But for those who were harmed, the resulting injuries are devastating.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The full costs of the VDPS have now been revealed , external for the first time in the answer to a parliamentary question from the backbench Conservative MP Sir Christopher Chope.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: In response, health minister Dame Diana Johnson said a total of £83m had been spent on staffing costs, administration and medical reviews between April 2022 and March 2026.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: Under the scheme, claimants must have their application reviewed by an independent doctor, to check whether they have met the threshold of "severe disablement".
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: If approved, they can then receive a one-off, tax-free payment of £120,000.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The process can take months or even years.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The costs of those medical assessments have increased from £4.3m in 2022/23 to £19.3m in 2025/26, according to new data published by the government.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: Based on the latest available data up to June 2026, the total amount paid out in damages to those who died or were injured after being given a Covid vaccine has risen to £31.6m.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: "The administrative costs and medical assessor supplier costs of the VDPS are driven by the number of claims received," said the NHSBSA, which runs the scheme on behalf of the government.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: "We have seen a significant increase in the number of claims received since taking over administration of the VDPS in November 2021." The campaign group Vaccine Injured and Bereaved UK (VIBUK), which was set up to support families affected, said the scheme was not fit for purpose.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: "It offers too little, too late, to too few and the cost of running it shows how inefficient it is," said the group's representative Kate Scott, whose husband Jamie was left severely disabled by the AstraZeneca Covid vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: Scott called on the government to act on the recommendations from module four of the Covid public inquiry and reform the scheme.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: Earlier this year, the Covid inquiry's chair, Baroness Heather Hallett, recommended increasing the payout and basing it on the degree of injury suffered.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The government is due to respond to her recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The BBC has previously reported on the large sums paid to an external medical provider which has been carrying out medical assessments.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: The Taxpayers' Alliance, a right-leaning think tank which campaigns for lower taxes and spending, said that the public would be "stunned" that the running costs of the scheme appeared to be "far more than has actually been paid out to those harmed".
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: "When administrative costs are running into tens of millions, ministers need to explain why the system is so expensive and whether victims are getting value from it," said the organisation's chief executive John O'Connell.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: "In the meantime, we are working to speed up claims and improve the experience for applicants," the government said.
sentences.article_title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims

sentences.text: NHSBSA said it continued to work "closely" with the government on "managing the costs of the VDPS".

sentences.text: Around 400 million people now live in countries which have legalised assisted dying.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Spain and Austria are among those which have changed the law in recent years, with some allowing help to die for those who are not terminally ill.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Just last month, France adopted an 'aid in dying' law for adults with incurable conditions causing them unbearable pain.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: While most jurisdictions forbid medical help to die, assisted dying laws around the world vary.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Across the US, assisted dying - which some critics prefer to call assisted suicide - is legal in 13 out of 50 states, as well as in Washington DC.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Oregon was one of the first places in the world to offer help to die for some patients, in 1997, and so has nearly 30 years' experience.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It has become the model on which other US assisted dying laws have been framed.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In Oregon, assisted dying is open to terminally ill , external , mentally competent adults expected to die within six months - and must be signed off by two doctors.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Since 1997 , external , 5,520 people have received a prescription for a lethal dose of medication - with 3,691 deaths.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In a 2025 report , external , 61% of patients who ask for help to die had cancer, 14% had a neurological condition like motor neurone disease and 11% had heart disease.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Around one in three of those prescribed a lethal dose don’t go ahead with it.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Oregon is important for supporters of assisted dying in England and Wales as they point out it has remained restricted to terminally ill adults since its introduction.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: However, opponents say some of the rules have been relaxed.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: A residency requirement has been lifted, which means it is open to people from outside the state.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The number of assisted deaths has also risen substantially over the years.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Canada is the country often cited by opponents of assisted dying as an example of the so-called "slippery slope" - a place where assisted dying has been extended and made available to more people since it was first brought in.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Medical assistance in dying (Maid) , external was introduced in 2016, initially just for the terminally ill.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: This was amended in 2021 and extended to those experiencing "unbearable suffering" from an irreversible illness or disability.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It had been due to be extended to people with a mental illness but that is now on hold.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Critics say the more the law is widened, the more disabled and vulnerable people will be put at risk.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: There has also been a dramatic growth in the number of people using Maid.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Roughly one in every 20 deaths in Canada are now medically assisted , external , compared to about one in 100 in Oregon.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Across Europe, several countries have legalised assisted dying: Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Spain, Austria, Portugal and, most recently, France.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Eligibility criteria vary widely.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Some jurisdictions allow assisted dying for people who are not terminally ill, while others, including France, restrict it to adults with serious incurable illnesses nearing the end of life.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Portugal's law was approved in 2023 but is not yet in force because of court and regulatory delays.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In 2025, Tuscany became the first region of Italy to establish a legal process for medically assisted suicide.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Earlier rulings by the constitutional courts in both Italy and Germany removed criminal penalties for assisted suicide in certain circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The Netherlands and Belgium both legalised assisted dying more than 20 years ago for patients experiencing unbearable suffering from an incurable illness, including mental health issues.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It has since been extended to children - the only European countries to allow this.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Both allow euthanasia - or physician-assisted dying.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Spain and Austria legalised assisted dying for both terminal illness and intolerable suffering in 2021 and 2022, respectively.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In Austria, the drugs must be self-administered, whereas in Spain a medical professional can administer them.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In England, Wales and Scotland, parliament has so far rejected assisted dying proposals.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: But assisted dying has already been legalised in one part of the British Isles.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In July, Royal Assent was given to a bill in Jersey.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Unlike at Westminster and Holyrood, the legislation was introduced by the Jersey government, which says it will take about 18 months to set up the service.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The first assisted death could happen late next year.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: There will be a residency requirement of one year, in a bid to prevent so-called 'death tourism'.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The measure, which most sets apart the Jersey legislation from the rest of the British Isles, concerns the manner in which those eligible for an assisted death can end their lives.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Individuals will be able to choose to have a doctor administer a lethal dose intravenously, as happens in Spain, Canada, New Zealand and most of Australia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: This is, in effect, voluntary euthanasia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It has become the preferred method of assisted dying in jurisdictions which allow this choice.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The laws proposed at Westminster, Holyrood and Tynwald - Isle of Man - all state that death must be by self-administration, which usually means the individual swallowing a lethal dose.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The Isle of Man assisted dying bill was passed by Tynwald (the Manx parliament) in March last year.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: As a UK Crown Dependency - like Jersey - it could not become law until granted Royal Assent.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: This was declined earlier this year by the UK Ministry of Justice, but Tynwald has since passed an updated bill which has been sent back to the UK government for a second time.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: If Royal Assent is granted, the Isle of Man expects the service to be operational next year.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: There is a residency requirement of five years.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In the past few years voluntary assisted dying has become legal across most of Australia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Last month, the Northern Territory parliament became the last part of Australia to pass Voluntary Assisted Dying legislation.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In New Zealand, patients must be terminally ill and expected to die within six months.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: That is extended to 12 months for those with a neurodegenerative condition in much of Australia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In both countries, patients can self-administer the lethal medication.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: But it can also be administered by a doctor or nurse, usually via an intravenous injection.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In South America, Uruguay passed a law in 2025 to permit assisted dying for adults with an incurable or terminal illness.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Across Latin America, Colombia, Ecuador and Cuba have decriminalised euthanasia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Additional reporting by Anthony Reuben and Gerry Georgieva
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the impact on partners - and what you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Prof Ama Johal, a consultant orthodontist and sleep expert at Aerox Health, explains that the partner of a snorer can become "so impacted upon that it's almost a last-ditch effort on their part to get up and go sleep in a separate room because they have to sleep".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: He adds: "As humans we physically can't function without that necessity." Prof Ama Johal says many couples put up with the negative effects snoring for too long During the night, we cycle through different stages of sleep in repeating patterns, usually every 90 minutes.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: The deeper stages of this cycle are important for physical restoration.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If sleep is frequently disrupted, you may spend less time in the restorative stages, meaning you can wake up feeling tired, even if you've spent a lot of time in bed, the BSSAA explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Your brain processes and stores information from the day during sleep.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Fragmented sleep - which can happen if you're waking up due to a snoring partner - can interrupt this process, impacting your focus and memory.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Disrupted sleep can also impact hormone regulation, which affects your energy levels and motivation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sleep also plays a role in regulating the brain systems involved in stress and emotional response.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: When it is disrupted, these systems can become less balanced, which may make you feel more irritable and less able to cope with stress.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: This is something Meg Warren, 29, experienced when her former partner's snoring would keep her up.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says: "Without fail, after a snoring-induced wake up I would feel on incredibly high alert." Meg, a charity media officer, would prod him throughout the night and try to coax him from his back to his side.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says she would wake up "feeling groggy and dazed, sometimes so much so that it would feel like a hangover".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Meg Warren felt 'groggy and dazed' after a night of little sleep due to her former partner's snoring Anna-Louise Dearden, a 52-year-old journalist, says she sometimes sleeps in a separate room from her partner due to his snoring.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Having this option allows her to prioritise getting enough rest when the snoring is particularly bad.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: There are things that can be done, say both Simon and Johal.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But first, it is important to distinguish whether your partner is simply snoring, or whether they have sleep apnoea.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "What you don't want to do is simply make someone quieter at night while potentially missing an underlying sleep-related breathing disorder," Simon says.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Signs of sleep apnoea, a disorder that causes a person's breathing to repeatedly stop and start during sleep, include pauses in breathing, choking at night, waking frequently, and suffering from morning headaches.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If this is what you are dealing with, you could be recommended a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machine, or even surgical treatment in some cases, Simon explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: For simple snoring, Simon said that lifestyle changes can make a difference, such as losing weight, stopping smoking, reducing alcohol intake before bed, or changing your sleeping position - such as laying on your side rather than your back.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: You can also suggest to your partner that they see a GP, who will be able to advise further or refer you to a specialist.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: An expert might suggest treating nasal obstruction or allergies, if this is what is causing snoring, or wearing a custom mouthguard to gently push the lower jaw forward and keep the airway open.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Johal says too many couples put up with snoring "for too long", which impacts their relationships and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "The key thing is that there is help out there, it's just tapping into it." How sleep tracking can make your sleep worse The hidden cost of the night shift and how to sleep it off
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Hugo was strangled to death while staying in an NHS mental health unit Staff falsified records, slept and were on their phones on the night one patient was killed by another on an NHS mental health unit in east London, an inquest has heard.
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: Hugo Flint Cahan, 34, was being treated at Newham Mental Health Centre (NMHC), run by the East London NHS Trust (ELFT), when he was fatally attacked by 22-year-old Rolando Torres-Pena.
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: Hugo's family say they have been shocked by the "dangerous" failures in his care.
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: The Trust says it has undertaken a significant programme of work to "improve our inpatient culture, behaviours and practice".
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: In a narrative conclusion, the coroner found Hugo was unlawfully killed which was contributed to by neglect, recommended four members of staff be referred to their regulator and that the Metropolitan police review their investigation into what happened that night.
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: Hugo, who had been a patient at the NHMC for six months, was strangled in the early hours of 3 January 2023 by Torres-Pena who had arrived on the ward five days earlier.
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: Torres-Pena pleaded guilty at the Old Bailey to manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility.
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: He was given a hospital order without time limit .
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: A coroner criticised repeated failures by the Trust in a number of patient deaths - not just Hugo's.
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: Graeme Irvine, the Senior Coroner for East London, said it was like "ground hog day" as he heard evidence of "the same" errors,  "over and over again," including the falsification of patient observation records and slow emergency responses.
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: CCTV footage shows the last image of Hugo alive On the night of Hugo's death, there were two nurses and a nursing assistant on duty on Topaz ward – an inpatient unit for men with acute mental health issues.

sentences.text: Torres-Pena was pacing the corridor believing he was about to leave, the inquest was told.
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: CCTV shows him following one of the nurses at one point.

sentences.text: When asked why he feels comfortable offering procedures that are concerning surgeons, Hussain says he "totally understands" why some are worried.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "It comes from the right place, that nervousness," he says, "but at the same time, more and more evidence is growing and we're getting the results" and that "there is a benefit" to men.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Hussain says he has an "immediate action plan" including drugs to quickly dissolve the filler in the event that things go wrong, and reports that "thankfully, we've never needed to" - although the BBC cannot independently corroborate that.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: But he recalls one patient who came to him for advice after treatment elsewhere, which had "really gone wrong".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He says the incorrect type of filler had been used and the "shaft of the penis was starting to become black" as the procedure had damaged the blood vessels in the penis and the skin was dying.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: The man was sent straight to A&E.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Prof Vaibhav Modgil has seen men for whom penis enhancement procedures have gone wrong Prof Vaibhav Modgil, an andrologist and consultant urological surgeon for the NHS in Manchester, has seen these men coming into hospital after botched procedures.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "When it does happen, it can be devastating for the patient," he says.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He recalls seeing men with "skin necrosis, where an area of the skin dies off it turns very black and then it sort of sloughs off.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "So, men will go in thinking, 'Oh, it's gonna be brilliant', but they might come out actually being even more dissatisfied than when they went in." Alex, who did not want his real name to be used, travelled to Germany for a different type of penis enhancement procedure.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He had surgery to cut the ligament that attaches the penis to the pubic bone to make it appear longer.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He also had his own fat cells harvested and injected into his penis to enlarge it.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: When he woke up after the procedure, he was in so much pain he couldn't stand.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "I sustained a lot of bruising and all my upper legs turned yellow," Alex says.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "I couldn't walk properly for about a month." Alex was treated in Modgil's clinic where eventually he was given the all-clear.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "Many people do not get that luxury," he says.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "I got off lucky." Alex says he knows he was "never small in the first place", but society and porn had convinced him that a bigger penis was "masculine and the best".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: There is a lack of data on how fillers affect the penis long-term Despite a lack of official data on the number of penile enhancement procedures, Modgil says online search trends, advertising and social media all "points to the fact that the numbers are on the up".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: This has led the British Association of Urological Surgeons to issue new recommendations against these procedures.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "The guidance that we've recently produced essentially says we cannot recommend that any of these procedures should take place because the evidence is so poor," says Modgil.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: It looked at 36 studies, involving 3,750 men, but said it was still not clear what the "safety profile" of these procedures were.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: This is partly down to a lack of data on how fillers affect the penis long-term.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: But there is also concern that - just like lip fillers - you do not need any qualifications to perform the procedure.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Modgil says an outright ban is "probably too severe", but if these procedures are going to continue then the industry "massively needs regulation".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He called for a national registry to record when penis filler procedures have been performed and for long-term data to be collected so men can make an informed decision based on the risks and the benefits.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Back in Manchester, Jason is happy with the results of his procedure and thinks he'll do it again when his current fillers wear off.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Sara Kahsai wants all survivors of FGM to seek help and not suffer alone Sara Kahsai grew up in Sudan but moved to Birmingham, England, in 2022 after marrying a bus driver from the city.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But as she settled into married life and her new home, she was coming to terms with a life-changing discovery.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara realised she was a victim-survivor of Female Genital Mutiliation (FGM), a procedure she had endured as a young girl.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was floored by the revelation and, not least, the excruciating pain she was now beginning to fully understand.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "The shock was massive," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It made it difficult with my physical relationship with my husband - but he was very kind and very patient with me." Warning: This story contains descriptions of the practices involved in female genital mutilation Sara turned to the one person she knew must have orchestrated it - her mother - and asked her why.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It was the culture to do it for everybody," she said her mother, still living in Africa, told her.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When I spoke to my mum she was really upset and she apologised to me." FGM involves the partial or total removal of female genitalia for non-medical reasons, and is practiced in some parts of Africa, the Middle East and Asia.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It also happens within some migrant communities in the UK, where it is illegal and treated as child abuse.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It is also against the law to take a girl abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Reasons include social acceptance, religion, misconceptions about hygiene and preserving a girl or woman's virginity.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The Home Office website cites World Health Organisation figures showing three million girls undergo some form , external of the procedure every year in Africa alone.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The mum received help for her FGM after she found out she was pregnant When Sara fell pregnant, she finally told health professionals she had endured FGM as a child.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was immediately referred to the specialist FGM Clinic, run by midwives at Birmingham Women's Hospital.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif deals with around 200 cases each year and says her job is to ensure the wellbeing of women and safeguard unborn children.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "Some types of female circumcision can affect the vaginal delivery," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: They offer deinfibulation - a procedure that can be carried out during pregnancy to separate fused tissue and enable safer births.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: What is FGM, where does it happen and why?
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Victim-survivors of FGM can also experience difficulty with urinating and menstruating, the midwife said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Women are more prone to infections and sepsis, and can suffer from severe and ongoing pain, as well having to deal with psychological trauma, anxiety and depression.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Many patients find it hard to talk to her about what's happened to them, Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It is very difficult, very emotional.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's very difficult for the woman to actually come forward and to come to the clinic, attend the clinic, and have a conversation with me as well," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I explain to them that I'm here to help and I try to explain to them what happened to them when they were a child." She said most women leave the clinic with a better understanding of how they have been affected and how they can take back control of their bodies.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "We talk about every part, what that part is there for and what's been removed and what cause for concern and what effect this will have for the rest of her life," Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Counselling is also offered as well as information on how partners and husbands can support them.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif runs the FGM centre at Birmingham Women's Hospital In 2015, children's charity Barnardo's set up the National FGM Centre to help better protect women and girls.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It works to prevent FGM, raise awareness of it and support those affected.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The centre said schools are legally required to teach pupils about FGM and the law surrounding it as part of relationships and sex education.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But how it is delivered can vary between schools.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's also not mandatory for it to be taught in primary schools and they want to see that change.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "For us, a huge part of tackling FGM is prevention," Rohma Ullah, from the centre, said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Among improvements on the way are new guidelines to help identify girls at risk of being taken abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara wants to urge other women in a similar position to take immediate action.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I have a message to all ladies who've had FGM," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When they come to the UK it is different.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: There's help here - go to their GP, seek help, ask for help.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "If I knew I could seek help I would not have waited until I was expecting... because I did suffer a lot before." If you have been affected by the contents of the article, support is available through the BBC Action Line website .
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Periods of hot weather can affect anyone, but some people run a greater risk of serious harm.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Experts recommend that those who may be more vulnerable - such as older people and babies and young children - should take extra precautions.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: As the body gets hotter, blood vessels open up.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This lowers your blood pressure and makes your heart work harder to push the blood around the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This process can cause mild symptoms such as an itchy heat rash or swollen feet.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: At the same time, sweating leads to the loss of fluids and salt and, crucially, the balance between them in the body changes.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This, combined with the lowered blood pressure, can lead to heat exhaustion.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Symptoms include: If blood pressure drops too far, the risk of heart attacks rises.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: How does sunscreen work, and how much do you need to use?
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Staying safe in water when the weather's hot Our bodies strive to keep a core temperature of about 37C whether we are in a snowstorm or a heatwave.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: That is the temperature at which our bodies have evolved to work.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: But as the weather gets hotter, it is harder for the body to keep its core temperature down.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: It opens more blood vessels near the skin to lose heat to our surroundings and starts sweating.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: As the sweat evaporates, it dramatically increases the heat lost from the skin.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: No one - especially babies, young children and animals - should ever be left in a locked vehicle.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Hot weather: How to sleep in the heat Six ways to keep your home and yourself cool in hot weather When is it too hot to walk your dog?
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: If you see someone you think has heat exhaustion , the NHS says you should: , external move them to a cool place get them to lie down and raise their feet slightly get them to drink plenty of water - sports or rehydration drinks are also OK cool their skin - spray or sponge them with cool water and fan them.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Cold packs around the armpits or neck are also good If they can be cooled down within half an hour, then heat exhaustion is not normally serious.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, if they do not recover within 30 minutes, then they are at risk of heatstroke .
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This is a medical emergency and you should call 999 immediately.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People with heatstroke may stop sweating even though they are too hot.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Their temperature could go over 40C and they might have seizures or lose consciousness.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: What to do if you think someone has heat exhaustion or heatstroke People who are older or have some long-term conditions - such as heart disease -  are sometimes less able to cope with the strain heat puts on the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Diabetes can make the body lose water more quickly and some complications of the disease can alter blood vessels and the ability to sweat.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Children and those who are less mobile may also be more vulnerable.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Brain diseases, such as dementia, can also leave people unaware of the heat or unable to do anything about it.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People who are homeless will also be more exposed to the sun.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Those living in top-floor flats will also face higher temperatures.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Yes - but the NHS says people should keep taking their medication as normal, and focus on staying cool and hydrated.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Diuretics - sometimes called "water pills" - increase the amount of water the body expels.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: They are taken widely, including for heart failure.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: In high temperatures, they increase the dangers of dehydration and imbalances in key minerals in the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Antihypertensives - which lower blood pressure - can combine with the blood vessels that are dilating to cope with the heat and cause dangerous drops in blood pressure.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Some drugs for people with epilepsy and Parkinson's can block sweating and make it harder for the body to cool itself.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Other drugs such as lithium or statins can become more concentrated and problematic in the blood if there is too much fluid loss.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: During 2022 - which saw the highest recorded temperature in England at 40.3C - there were an estimated 2,985 so-called "excess deaths" as a result of the heat , external , the most recorded in any given year.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: There were an estimated 1,311 heat-associated deaths , external during summer 2024, and an estimated 1,504 , external during summer 2025.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Most heat-related excess deaths are due to heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: The higher death rate starts to kick in once the thermometer passes 25C-26C.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, evidence suggests the deaths tend to be caused by higher temperatures in spring or early summer rather than during "peak summer".
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This could be because we start to change our day-to-day behaviour as summer progresses and we get more used to dealing with the heat.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: The evidence from previous heatwaves is the increase in deaths happens very quickly - within the first 24 hours of a heatwave.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Martine Barons who began lifting weights during lockdown is now a three-time world champion A 65-year-old grandmother has become a three-time world champion powerlifter after only starting the sport two and a half years ago.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Martine Barons, from Stratford-upon-Avon, said she began lifting weights during lockdown after listening to a seminar that said women going through menopause should run less and lift more.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Her colleague at the University of Warwick, who is also a personal trainer, then showed Barons how to deadlift, and spotted her potential.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons is now nicknamed The Deadlifting Grandma.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: On Monday, she won at the AWPC World Powerlifting Championships in the 65 to 85 age group, becoming a three-time world champion, after starting out entering competitions just for fun.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said she has seen a "huge change" in her physique and capabilities "I have seen such a huge change in my own physique and my capabilities – I am sure that my body is at least 20 years younger," she told BBC CWR.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "When they invited me to the British and European Championships, I thought, 'Well I have been invited it would be rude not to go', but who thought it would lead to this?
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said her journey, down to hard work and dedication over the past couple of years, has been "so exciting".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "I have learnt so much, I have met people all around the world, and it has been delightful," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: For women who want to get fit and improve their strength, Baron said there were lots of options, one route is to join a gym and develop a tailored programme with a coach.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Alternatively, Baron said those who prefer more privacy could "start really gently at home with some resistance bands and a programme".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: She added her powerlifting has led to having more capability on a day-to-day basis, along with now being able to touch her toes first thing in the morning.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "If I need to move furniture at home, I can do that, I can toss my grandchildren in the air, I can play games with them," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "My posture is better and I just feel more capable and more confident in everyday life".

sentences.text: The Health Improvement Commission for Guernsey and Alderney said residents would receive the scorecard through their letterbox An alcohol consumption campaign with scorecards to monitor units, is aimed at helping islanders make informed decisions about their health.

sentences.text: The Rethink Your Drink scheme, set up by the Health Improvement Commission for Guernsey and Alderney, encourages residents to fill in scorecards noting their weekly alcohol intake and compare the results to the recommended guidelines.

sentences.text: The charity said islanders will receive a scorecard through their letterbox.
sentences.article_title: Alcohol consumption scorecard to help track intake

sentences.text: Andrea Nightingale, substance use lead at the Health Improvement Commission, said the scorecard was "a simple, interactive and engaging way to help people understand their intake".
sentences.article_title: Alcohol consumption scorecard to help track intake

sentences.text: The UK Chief Medical Officers' low-risk drinking guidelines , external recommend men and women drink no more than 14 units per week, spread over three or more days, with at least two alcohol-free days each week.

sentences.text: The commission added alcohol units can be difficult to estimate, so the scorecard provides "a tried and tested tool" to help people calculate their weekly units and compare their results to the guidelines.
sentences.article_title: Alcohol consumption scorecard to help track intake

sentences.text: Nightingale said: "The scorecard is about helping people get a clearer picture of where they are today and giving them the confidence to think about where they would like to be tomorrow.
sentences.article_title: Alcohol consumption scorecard to help track intake
